chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, from Musa ibn Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') who arrives in Mecca on the night of Arafah. He said: 'He has no Tamattu' (benefit); he makes it a single Hajj, and he performs Tawaf around the House, and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and he goes out to Mina, and there is no Hadi (sacrificial animal) upon him. Indeed, the Hadi is only upon the Mutamatti'.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One who performs Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who arrives in Mecca on the night of Arafah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific fiqh scenario where a pilgrim intending Hajj al-Tamattu' arrives in Mea on the night of Arafah, effectively converting their status to Hajj al-Mufrad. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that they perform the rituals of Mufrad—Tawaf and Sa'i—without the obligation of Hadi, as the sacrificial animal is strictly tied to the distinct state of Tamattu' which requires remaining in Mecca until the Day of Sacrifice. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing of ihram and the distinct legal obligations associated with each form of Hajj.
